narrows: Route 43's 'the flattening the extended Bloch group needs is already a theorem in the corpus'. The y-level identity is unchanged; the claim that the branch data IS the flattening does not generalise -- the placement differs at w and fails at c.

gates.claim: the tower carries a branch relation at EVERY level and all three are integral: eps = (+1,-1,0) at y, eta = (-1,+1,0) at w, delta = (-2,+2,0) at c. So the raw material Route 43 used exists everywhere -- which is what makes the failure in G3 a real negative rather than a missing input

ROUTE 43'S y-LEVEL RESULT STANDS, exact and unchanged: branch data in the p slot gives sum Rhat = -1 unit of pi^2/6. Nothing below retracts this -- what is narrowed is the claim that the same recipe is what the extended Bloch group wants in general

THE NEGATIVE, and it narrows my own Route 43 claim. Branch data in the p slot gives an integer multiple of pi^2/6 ONLY at the y level. At w the integer-valued flattening lives in the q slot instead, and at c the single hit over [-3,3] is (1,-1) -- neither +delta nor -delta. The PLACEMENT is therefore not determined by the branch relation and does not transfer up the tower, so 'the flattening is supplied by the cubic' holds at y and is not a law

THE STRUCTURE. The branch relation is a NULL direction of the flattening correction: 3*log(1-y_3) - 2*log(y_3) = 0 at the real root, so shifting (p_3,q_3) by (3,-2) changes the total by nothing. Flattenings are a TORSOR modulo the branch relation, not distinguished tuples -- which is why three different (p_3,q_3) give the identical sum, and why 'is eps THE flattening' was the wrong question to ask of it

how rare the integer flattenings are, reported rather than implied: 6 hits at y, 6 at w, 1 at c over p,q in [-3,3] with the conjugate root carrying the conjugate flattening. Route 43 found eps by exactly this kind of search and only then recognised it, so the search's yield belongs in the record

verdict.stands: sum_sigma Rhat(y_sigma; eps_sigma, 0) = -pi^2/6 at the y level, exact.
verdict.narrowed: the recipe does not transfer up the tower. Branch data in the p slot is integral only at y; w needs the q slot, c matches neither.
verdict.structure: the branch relation is a null direction of the flattening correction, so flattenings form a torsor modulo it. 'Is eps the flattening' is the wrong question -- only its class can be.
verdict.next: Neumann's parity/geometric conditions are still NOT imposed. Getting them in is what would pick the class out, and it is now clearly the blocking step rather than a formality.
